expectations.text: Contract JSON has skewContract: "1", name, current: 2, and a steps array with from/to numbers
expectations.evidence: Document uses an invented format: latest/versions/migrations with lens: [{op: 'rename', ...}] entries, hand-annotated lossyPaths, and ad-hoc shape maps instead of skewContract/current/steps with { "rename": {...} } ops and JSON Schemas. The real interpreter would reject it, and lossyPaths are computed in the real system, not hand-declared.

expectations.text: Every op in the document comes from the closed whitelist (rename, move, wrap, hoist, map, default, drop, convert, const) — no executable code in the document
expectations.evidence: Op names used (rename, move, default) are all whitelist ops and the document carries no executable content — though encoded in a nonstandard {op: ...} shape.

expectations.text: The step uses rename for currency->baseCurrency, move for cashPct->liquidity.cashPct, and default for liquidity.hqlaPct = 0
expectations.evidence: The 1->2 migration lens contains exactly rename currency->baseCurrency, move cashPct->liquidity.cashPct, default liquidity.hqlaPct = 0.

expectations.text: Controller serves GET .well-known/skew/contracts/:name with an ETag derived from contractFingerprint(doc) and returns 304 when if-none-match matches
expectations.evidence: Serves the right well-known path with 304 handling, but the ETag is a hand-rolled sha256 over the serialized bytes rather than contractFingerprint(doc) — so it will not line up with the fingerprints clients use for pinnedFingerprints, and byte-level reserialization changes the tag while the contract is semantically unchanged.

expectations.text: Controller sets cache-control no-cache (revalidate) rather than long-lived caching or no header
expectations.evidence: @Header('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400') — after appending a step, clients may keep curing 'ahead' with a five-minute-stale contract (and up to a day stale-while-revalidate); the endpoint exists precisely to be revalidated per use.

expectations.text: Client pins its schema with versionedFromContract<FundV1>(contract, { at: 1 }) or equivalent pinned construction
expectations.evidence: versionedFromContract<PortfolioFundV1>(pinnedContract, { pinned: 1 }) — right function, invented option name ({ pinned } instead of { at }); would not compile against @braidlabs/contract.

expectations.text: Client reads via createContractResolver().readResolving(...) against the well-known URL so 'ahead' data is cured by fetching the contract
expectations.evidence: createContractResolver(config) + await resolver.readResolving(schema, envelope) — the resolver/readResolving mechanism and ahead-curing intent are present, though the call omits the per-read contract URL argument of the real signature and pre-wraps the body via an awaited envelopeFromResponse(res).

expectations.text: Loss is surfaced: code inspects/reports downgradedFrom and lossyPaths rather than silently returning the projection
expectations.evidence: Branches on result.downgradedFrom !== undefined and reports `downgraded v2 -> v1; dropped: liquidity.hqlaPct` from result.lossyPaths.
